initial_condition_comparison.ratio: 10x lower than paper initial perturbation amplitude
initial_condition_comparison.disposition: same linear-Landau physical parameters apart from amplitude; not an exact paper-initial-condition reproduction

exploratory_peak_fit.method: find local extrema of absolute value of signed imaginary fundamental electric-field Fourier coefficient in the sampled trace; regress ln(peak magnitude) against peak time

four_extrema_fit.note: Descriptive fit only; conventional iid-regression interval is not an uncertainty statement for a deterministic numerical trajectory.

exploratory_peak_fit.note: Exploratory post-transient peak-envelope slope is close to the paper-reported linear Landau rate, but the fit window was selected after observing this run, uses only four post-initial extrema, and the perturbation amplitude differs by 10x. No validated reproduction or SOTA claim.

refinement_probe.interpretation: same independent spatial, velocity-grid, velocity-domain, and timestep sweeps as prior run; the t=10 Landau run uses a single 64x128 grid

caveats: The trace is a numerical reference-prototype diagnostic, not a continuum accuracy certification.
The long-horizon envelope fit is exploratory and must not be described as a validated Landau damping reproduction.
The 0.001 perturbation is ten times smaller than the paper-reported VlasovTT Landau amplitude 0.01.
The finite periodic velocity interval is truncated.
The spectral-tail and Nyquist fractions are observed occupancy diagnostics, not truncation-error certificates.
The x/v grid was not refined at t=10, so this run does not establish long-horizon grid convergence.
No production solver runtime, memory or energy advantage was measured.
